# Write a clean subject on the first line, without a label prefix.
# Start with a capitalized action verb. Aim for 50 characters.
# Leave a blank line before the body. Wrap body text at 72 characters.
Subject

Why:

How:

Tags:

# Why, How and Tags are all required.
# Why: say why this change is needed.
# How: say how it addresses that need. Keep claims within the evidence.
# Tags: Bug, Enhancement.
# Choose any that apply, including both Bug and Enhancement when both apply.
# Use None alone when none fits. All other labels stay out.
# Tags belong in the body, not before the subject.
# Never put private conversation references, secrets or personal details here.
# Delete prompts and comments from the finished message.
# These verbs are choices, not words every commit must contain:
# Create = Bring in something new, such as a feature, test or dependency.
# Remove = Take something out, such as a feature, test or dependency.
# Fix = Fix an issue e.g. bug, typo, accident, misstatement.
# Bump = Increase the version of something e.g. a dependency.
# Build = Change the build process, tools or infrastructure.
# Enable = Turn on an existing feature or setting.
# Disable = Turn off an existing feature or setting without removing it.
# Optimize = A change that MUST be just about performance, e.g. speed up code.
# Document = A change that MUST be only in the documentation, e.g. help files.
# Refactor = A change that MUST be just refactoring.
# Reformat = A change that MUST be just format, e.g. indent line, trim space, etc.
# Rephrase = A change that MUST be just textual, e.g. edit a comment, doc, etc.
#
# Adapted from git-commit-template 7.2.0 by Joel Parker Henderson.
